en.title: Sölden next week: light snow only, 13 cm up high (snow forecast 23–29 November 2026)
en.description: Sölden snow forecast for 23–29 November 2026: 13 cm at the top (2–24 cm), 8 cm at the base, snowiest day Thursday 26 November, with neighbours compared.
en.lede: Sölden gets a small share of next week's snow: 13 cm at around 3100 m in the middle of our forecast, 12 cm at mid-mountain and 8 cm down at 1400 m. The best of it should come on Thursday 26 November.

sections.h: What falls where on the Sölden slopes
p: Our forecast splits Sölden's week like this: upper slopes 13 cm (low 2, high 24), middle of the mountain 12 cm, lower runs 8 cm (low 1, high 15).
Most of the total arrives on Thursday 26 (5 cm, up to 9), counted at the top as the middle of our forecast and the high case.
Little lands in Sölden before the weekend: 10 cm at the top from Tuesday 17 to Friday 20 November. Most of what the resort gets this fortnight comes in the second week.
Half-and-half at the bottom: 8 cm near 1400 m is a fair amount, but well short of the top's 13 cm. Mild spells will turn the lowest runs heavy and sticky.
Sölden opens on its glaciers in autumn, so it is often the first big Austrian area to ski.

sections.h: Where the good snow will be
p: The snowiest day up top is Thursday 26 November, with 5 cm in the middle of our forecast (up to 9 cm). That is a fresh coat on the groomers, nothing more.

Go high: depth is safest on the Rettenbach and Tiefenbach glaciers, and the best skiing should be on the two glaciers and the Gaislachkogl's upper slopes. Treat the village in the Ötztal valley as the weak point.
For comparison, the upper slopes of the closest big resorts collect Obergurgl (10 km away) 13 cm, Stubai Glacier (12 km away) 14 cm and Ischgl (49 km away) 18 cm; Sölden sits at 13 cm.
Nothing to separate them on snow alone; the choice comes down to the terrain you want.

sections.h: The range, not just the number
p: Treat this one with caution: 2 cm at the low end, 24 cm at the high end. A spread that wide a week out means the storm may still slide away from Sölden or sit right over it.
Storm timing tends to firm up first; totals keep moving until a day or two before.

advice: Off the groomed runs, new snow means new avalanche risk: the regional avalanche service of the province is the reference.
Check the resort's own opening date and lift status: snow on the mountain does not mean lifts are running.
With 13 cm at the top, this is not a week to chase powder in Sölden.
